newsitem.title: USA: Ford Q1 up on cost-cutting measures.
newsitem.headline: Ford Q1 up on cost-cutting measures.

text.p: Ford Motor Co, which reported sharply higher first quarter earnings, on Wednesday said its cost-cutting measures were beginning to pay off.

"There's still much to do," Ford Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Alex Trotman said in a statement. "But our progress is encouraging, and the entire Ford team is focused on meeting our business objectives and making us an even stronger competitor."
Ford reported first quarter earnings of $1.20 per fully diluted share, beating the Wall Street consensus estimate of about $0.90 a share. A year ago, it earned $0.53.

In addition to cost cutting, Trotman attributed the first quarter earnings improvement to new, higher-margin products that Ford has introduced over the last two years. Ford's new products include the F-150 full-size pickup truck and Expedition full-size sport utility vehicle.

"The changes we have been making to our automotive operations for the past two years are beginning to pay off," Trotman said. "We have developed a very strong product lineup around the world, particularly in the fastest growing segments."
Trotman said the company is on track to meet its business objectives, assuming the economies of its major markets continue to perform as expected.
